```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

This script is aimed to explore and plot the number of Ensembl Regulatory Features identified with the Ensembl [Regulatory Build](https://regulation.ensembl.org/help/regulatory_build)
and released in [Ensembl 114](https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-114/regulation/). 


```{r, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(rtracklayer)
```

The first step is to download the files from the Ensembl FTP. This script will 
place them in the `~/Downloads/` folder. If you want to use this code, make 
sure you specified the correct path to your data folder.

```{r}
# replace with the full path to the folder where files will be downloaded
data_folder <- "~/Downloads/"

eFTP <- "https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-114/regulation"


species <- c('Homo_sapiens', 'Mus_musculus', 'Sus_scrofa', 'Gallus_gallus',
             'Bos_taurus', 'Salmo_salar', 'Scophthalmus_maximus', 
             'Dicentrarchus_labrax', 'Oncorhynchus_mykiss', 
             'Cyprinus_carpio_carpio')
names(species) <- c('Human', 'Mouse', "Pig", "Chicken", "Cattle", 
                    "Atlantic \n salmon", "Turbot", "European \n seabass", 
                    "Rainbow \n trout", "Common \n carp")
assemblies <- c('GRCh38', 'GRCm39', 'Sscrofa11.1', 'GRCg7b', 'ARS-UCD2.0',
                'Ssal_v3.1', 'ASM1334776v1', 'dlabrax2021', 'USDA_OmykA_1.1', 
                'Cypcar_WagV4.0')
```

```{r}
for(i in 1:length(species)){
  reg_file <- paste(species[i], assemblies[i],
                    "regulatory_features.v114.gff3.gz", sep = "." )
  dest_reg_file <- paste(data_folder, species[i], ".v114.gff3.gz", sep = '')
  download.file(paste(eFTP, tolower(species[i]), assemblies[i], "annotation",
                      reg_file, sep = "/"), destfile = dest_reg_file)
  system(paste('gzip -d ', dest_reg_file, sep = ''))
}
```

The next step is to import the regulatory features from the downloaded files,
and compute number of features per feature type and per species.

```{r}
rfs_summary <- NULL

for(i in 1:length(species)){
  readGFF(paste(data_folder, species[i], ".v114.gff3", sep = '')) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    group_by(type) %>%
    summarize(species_name = names(species)[i], n = n()) %>%
    bind_rows (rfs_summary) -> rfs_summary
}
```

Preparing the dataset to be plot.

```{r}
rfs_summary %>%
  mutate(species_name = factor(species_name, levels = names(species)),
         type = factor( type, levels = c("promoter", "enhancer",
                                         "CTCF_binding_site", 
                                         "open_chromatin_region" ),
                        labels = c("promoter",  "enhancer",
                                   "CTCF binding site", 
                                   "open chromatin" ))) -> rfs_summary

```

```{r, fig.height=5, fig.width=9, dpi = 300}
rf_colors <- c('promoter' = '#ff0000', 'enhancer' = '#faca00', 
            'CTCF binding site' = '#40e0d0', 'open chromatin' = '#d9d9d9')

rfs_summary %>%
  ggplot(aes (x = species_name, y = n, fill = type)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = 'identity', position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position.inside = c(0.9,0.9), legend.background = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(vjust = 0.5),
        panel.grid = element_blank()) + 
  labs(fill = '', x = '', y = 'Number of annotated regulatory regions') + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = rf_colors) + 
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 400000), breaks = seq(0, 400000, 50000),
                     expand = c(0,0)) -> Figure_1_b
Figure_1_b

```

Finally, we will export the data displayed in the bar plot.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
rfs_summary %>%
  #remove the '\n' character in the species names
  mutate( species_name = str_replace_all(species_name, "\n", "")) %>%
  write.table(paste(data_folder, 'rfs_summary.v114.tsv', sep = ''), 
              quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE)
```
